title: Twenty guessers, one test
hook: No model here knows anything. How well does the leaderboard winner score?

knows: why we hold out a test set (ten-test-cases)
that a score is a sample, so it varies by luck
doesNotKnow: that choosing the best of many models by the same test set turns that test set into training data, so the winner's score is inflated even when no model has any skill, and only a fresh test set shows it

misconception: The top score on a leaderboard measures the top model's real skill; if no model is any good, no model will score well.
objective: The learner can explain that the best of many skill-free models scores well above 50% on a shared test because picking the best picks the luckiest, that the lead vanishes on fresh questions, and that a final test set must be used only once.

claims.text: With 20 models that each guess, scored on the same 100 questions, the best score averages about 59 of 100 (exact 59.31); the learner's run is one sample (seed 1: 56).
claims.source: E[max of 20 Binomial(100, 0.5)] = sum over k of 1 - F(k)^20 = 59.31 (node, 2026-10-14); stage simulation board() in Demo.tsx averaged over seeds 1-20,000: 59.32. Seeds run 1, 2, 3, ... in press order, untuned; seed 1 is simply the first. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own exact sum over k of 1 − F(k)^20 with F = Binomial(100, 0.5) cdf: 59.31. Own node port of board() with mulberry32: seed 1, 20 models, winner 56 (seeds 1 to 40: 56 to 66). Default m = 20 and nextSeed = 1, so the first Run press is seed 1; if the learner presses a Models button first, seed 1 goes to that m (the claim calls seed 1 an example, which holds).

claims.text: The winner re-scored on fresh questions scores about 50% whatever it scored before: the lead was noise (seed 1: 49.7% on 1,000 fresh questions).
claims.source: The fresh questions are independent of the choice, so the winner is still a 50% guesser: expected 50%. fresh() in Demo.tsx (1,000 questions, mulberry32(seed + 100000)) averaged over seeds 1-20,000: 50.0%. Over seeds 1-5,000 the fresh score reached the winner's shared score in 6 runs; the reveal has a branch for that case. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own port of fresh(): seed 1 gives 49.7%; over seeds 1 to 2,000 the fresh score ranges 44.9% to 56.0%, mean 50.07%. It is independent of the shared test (a separate stream, mulberry32(seed + 100000)), so the winner stays a 50% guesser. The fresh score reached the winner's shared score in 4 of 2,000 seeds; the reveal has a branch for that ('a rare run where luck held'), so the stage never says 'fell' when it did not.

claims.text: The more models compete, the higher a skill-free winner climbs: on average about 50, 56, 59 and 62 of 100 for 1, 5, 20 and 100 models.
claims.source: Exact expected maxima 50.00, 55.81, 59.31, 62.48 (node, 2026-10-14). With one seed the first m models of a larger board are the same models, so on the stage the best of 100 is never below the best of 20 for that seed (seed 1: 53, 54, 56, 59). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own exact expected maxima: 50.00, 55.81, 59.31, 62.48 for m = 1, 5, 20, 100, which round to the claim's 50, 56, 59, 62. board(seed, m) shares a prefix across m, so for one seed the best of 100 is ≥ the best of 20 ≥ the best of 5 (seed 1: 53, 54, 56, 59). The reveal crowd lines are guarded by crowd.w ≥ r.w or ≤ r.w, so they never contradict the run.

claims.text: Using one test set to choose among many models quietly trains on it; keep a final test set that is used once, after the choice.
claims.source: Dwork, Feldman, Hardt, Pitassi, Reingold and Roth (2015), 'The reusable holdout: preserving validity in adaptive data analysis', Science 349(6248): 636-638; Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., section 7.2 (the test set kept 'in a vault' and used only at the end). About real systems; needs the fact-checker. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD UNVERIFIED. Reveal sentence matches the claim. The selection bias is shown on stage, but the claim is about practice with real models ('quietly trains on it'; 'keep a final test set ... used once') and rests on Dwork et al. 2015 (Science) and ESL 2nd ed. 7.2. Neither could be opened (WebFetch DNS failure for hastie.su.domains; proxy 403). Left unverified. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD. No source that supports it could be opened from this host: the cited hosts return proxy 403 or fail DNS, and only GitHub raw, PyPI and npm are reachable. I did not verify it from memory or from search snippets. Dwork et al. 2015 (Science) and ESL 2nd ed. 7.2 were not found on any reachable mirror. The selection bias itself is shown on stage (c1-c3, verified).
claims.note: FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Learner text (Demo.tsx line 105): 'Using one test set to choose among many models quietly trains on it. Keep a final test set that is used once, after the ...'. Opened on PMC: Patterns 2025 6(4): 101185, 'Unraveling overoptimism and publication bias in ML-driven science' (PMC12010447). It says 'Model development is inherently an iterative, adaptive process where researchers reuse test sets to refine models. However, repeated use of the same test set can lead to inadvertently learning specific patterns or noise unique to that set, exacerbating overfitting', and 'reusing a test set multiple times during model development introduces significant overfitting errors, which optimistically scales as [a function of] t / n' (formula as extracted from the HTML), citing Dwork et al. 2015 (holdout reuse). That supports the first sentence ('quietly trains on it'). The second, a test set used once after the choice, is the direct remedy: a set used once is not reused, so this bias cannot arise. Dwork et al. 2015 (Science) and ESL 7.2 are not opened; this paper is the basis.

claims.text: The models are a toy that only guess (each question right with chance 50%), labelled on the stage ('Toy models that only guess').
claims.source: Brief 58, company/domains/briefs/ai.ml-basics.md. Departure: the fresh test has 1,000 questions (brief: 100) so one run shows the fall to about 50%. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Stage tag text 'Toy models that only guess' (Demo.tsx span.tag) matches. The model: each question is right if r() < 0.5, for every model, on both tests. No skill parameter exists.

recall.question: A team tries 50 prompt variants and reports the one that scored best on their 200-question benchmark. What should you expect when it meets new questions?
options: It scores lower than reported, because the best of 50 was partly luck
It scores about the same, because the benchmark measured it
It scores higher, because it was the best
recall.why: Picking the best of many on one test set picks luck along with skill. Only a test used once, after the choice, gives an honest score.
